items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: I can play for you some of the things I did with Wilbur de Paris

ctx.x: And it's too bad the band never recorded.

And we didn't have to rehearse a tune. We'd say, 'Well, let's play this tune.' Everybody knew it. I tell my boys -- my students -- you never learn a melody unless you learn the harmony at the same time, because if you don't know the harmony, you don't know the music. You don't know it. So, everybody was familiar with the harmony of everything we played. And it was just fantastic how we could play four-part -- not three-part -- four-part harmony. Bingie Madison was a very qualified arranger. He was a master of…

salary, but I averaged -- and we worked seven nights a week, too, you see, and you had $130, $140, $150.00 a week. You could figure on that. And that was right during the depression. The depression started in '30, you know, because the crash was in '29, and that was in '30 when things were rough. Musicians were hungry. But we had that job -- so, something happened. Snowden- told him we wanted a raise. Said he wouldn't give it to us. So, we said, "Well, we quit." Snowden gave him his notice. So, it's time to quit,…
